frontier.name: Polynomial H² classification
frontier.text: : build the mode-block coefficient modules so the Whitehead lemmas normalise an arbitrary loop cocycle to vanish on constant loops. Combined with the mode recurrence, this classifies central extensions of the polynomial loop algebra.

frontier.name: Current topology
frontier.text: : give formal currents the t-adic linear topology. Prove Hausdorffness, completeness, continuity of the bracket and density of polynomial currents, which is the prerequisite for every continuous statement in A1.

frontier.name: Continuous cohomology and the residue cocycle on currents
frontier.text: : define continuous cochains with discrete coefficients and prove the joint-continuity criterion. Extend the residue pairing to a continuous cocycle cκ on g((t)), and add the coordinate invariance the scalar pairing still lacks.

frontier.name: The extension ĝκ and h∨
frontier.text: : construct the central extension with its continuous section and prove perfectness exactly when κ ≠ 0. Define h∨ intrinsically and prove Killing = 2h∨κ0 using the invariant-form uniqueness already proved.

frontier.name: Smooth-part coreflection and coinduction
frontier.text: : give the smooth-vector right adjoint and continuous coinduction, which yield `EnoughInjectives` and Ext for the smooth module category.

status.glance: Only foundations exist so far. The finite-dimensional inputs to the A1 classification are proved: the Whitehead lemmas, the fact that invariant forms are multiples of the Killing form, and the polynomial mode recurrence. So are the first carriers for formal currents, the residue pairing and smooth modules. Nothing from the affine extension ĝκ onward has begun, and neither headline theorem has been started: the scalar center away from critical level and Feigin–Frenkel.

frontier.name: Maximum principle on compact submanifolds (A1)
frontier.text: — show that a strictly plurisubharmonic function has no compact positive-dimensional complex submanifold in its domain. A3's dimension bound and A5's argument that A meets every component both need it.

frontier.name: Shape operators and paired focal distances (A2)
frontier.text: — derive S_νJ=−JS_ν and S_(Jν)=JS_ν from the existing B identities, then apply the anticommuting-spectrum theorem to get symmetric focal distances on each normal line. The input is the RiemannianGeometry R6 shape operator.

frontier.name: Affine CW dimension ≤ n (A2)
frontier.text: — move the squared-distance identities onto the GT Layer1 normal carrier, then combine properness, almost-every-point Morse genericity and MorseTheory M1–M2 to get a CW model with cells of index ≤ n.

frontier.name: Projective zero-locus carrier (A0)

frontier.name: Pseudoconvex exhaustion topology (A3)
frontier.text: — Morse-approximate a strongly q-pseudoconvex exhaustion with the fine-openness result above, then read off a CW dimension ≤ n+q and homology vanishing. MorseTheory M3–M4 has to supply this.

status.glance: A1, the Levi calculus and the real index bounds, is essentially done. The one gap is the maximum principle on compact complex submanifolds. A2 has its pointwise identities in flat coordinates and nothing global yet. The projective carriers (A0), pseudoconvex exhaustions (A3), Borel–Moore duality and triangulation (A4), the Lefschetz theorems (A5) and the examples (A6) have not begun.

frontier.text: — relative homology already vanishes below the connectivity of a pair ([`TauCeti.isZero_singularHomology_ofSubset_of_relHomotopyGroup`](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/AlgebraicTopology/Singular/Cubical/Compression/Relative.html#TauCeti.isZero_singularHomology_ofSubset_of_relHomotopyGroup)). frontier.text: — the classical and cubical Hurewicz maps are known to differ by a universal unit of `ℤ`, but the sign itself is not determined. The roadmap's orientation conventions ask for it to be fixed.

frontier.text: — the spectral sequence of a filtered space exists with finite convergence, and fibre bundles give Serre fibrations. What remains is the skeletal filtration of the total space and `E² = H_p(B; H_q(F))` with monodromy. Bundle Euler multiplicativity waits on it.

frontier.name: Algebraic spectral sequences

status.glance: Van Kampen, relative singular homology, and excision with Mayer–Vietoris (Stages 1–3) are done. The Jordan-curve topology that the revised roadmap places under L5 has separation but not, in general, exactly two complementary components. Prime ends have barely begun.

For every discrete Γ the compactified quotient is a Riemann surface, and it is now compact whenever a cuspidal polygon meets every orbit, but no such polygon is yet built for a general cofinite group. Much of the Poincaré polygon theorem is in place without the theorem itself. Genus and Riemann–Hurwitz have not begun.

frontier.text: — reduced and unreduced integer-graded theories and their equivalence can start now. They depend only on the pointed CW suppliers, not on the spectral model.

status.glance: Work so far is all foundations for G2. Most of the pointed simplicial category is in place: smash product, closed structure, tensors, circle, suspension and loops. The raw mapping-path fibration is largely built. Nothing in the library is yet a spectrum or a cohomology theory, and G1 and G3–G5 have not begun.

frontier.name: The scalar constancy criterion
frontier.text: — show that a distribution on a connected Euclidean open set whose derivatives all vanish is a constant multiple of Lebesgue integration. Locally constant regularizations are done. What remains is mollifier convergence in the test topology, to recover the distribution from its regularizations, and then matching the constants on overlapping balls.

frontier.name: The Euclidean constancy theorem for top-degree currents
frontier.text: — combine the top-degree zero-boundary reduction with the scalar criterion to show that such a current on a connected open set is a constant multiple of the integration current. This waits only on the criterion above.

frontier.name: The manifold carrier
frontier.text: — define `TestForm k M` and `Current k M` by specializing ComplexKahlerGeometry K5a's real bundle-test foundation. Prove the Euclidean chart comparison with the native test functions already in use here. The supplier is the main prerequisite.

frontier.name: Mass
frontier.text: — extended mass as a supremum over tests of comass at most one, local finite mass, and the Radon mass measure. This needs CalibratedGeometry C1's comass.

frontier.name: G2 onward
frontier.text: — integer-rectifiable and integral currents depend on G1's carrier and mass and on GeometricMeasureTheory G2–G6. Nothing here has started.

status.glance: Only Euclidean groundwork for G1 has landed so far. Test forms on open subsets of a finite-dimensional space have a continuous exterior derivative, the oriented integration current exists and has zero boundary, and distributions can be regularized by translation. The manifold carrier, mass, and every layer from G2 to G7 have not been started.

The augmenting-path optimality criterion and the lattice of minimum cuts are proved, and the walk, excess and residual layers are partly built. Max-flow/min-cut itself is not yet proved, since nothing shows a maximum flow exists. Bridges and blocks, Menger, ear decompositions, circulations and Gomory–Hu trees have not begun.

frontier.text: — for `kQ` with the path-length grading, identify the bigraded Ext-Euler form with the graded Ringel form. Then specialize at `q = 1` through the Ext comparison hypotheses. frontier.text: — prove that the classes of an exhaustive family of indecomposable graded projectives are linearly independent over `ℤ[q,q⁻¹]`, which completes the spanning result already proved.

rows.name: ModularForms

frontier.name: Atkin–Li pseudo-eigenvalues.
frontier.text: Define `λ_Q(f)` for proper exact divisors by `W_Q f = λ_Q(f)·g` with `g` the newform of character `χ̄_Q·χ_{N/Q}`, and prove `|λ_Q| = 1`. The square of `W_Q` and newspace stability are in place.

frontier.name: Galois stability.
frontier.text: Give the newspace Hecke algebra its `ℚ(χ)`-structure, then define `f^σ`. Orbit sizes and rational characteristic polynomials follow, and Layer 9 consumes them.

frontier.name: The Eisenstein decomposition.
frontier.text: Identify the common kernel of the constant terms at every cusp with `S_k(N, χ)` and show the Eisenstein series span the image. This also unlocks the sharp non-cuspidal abscissa.

frontier.name: Cross-level strong multiplicity one.
frontier.text: Compare newforms at unrelated levels; uniqueness of the primitive pair needs it.

frontier.name: The level-one trace formula.
frontier.text: Define Hurwitz class numbers, evaluate the remaining conjugacy contributions, and make the period-polynomial isomorphism Hecke-equivariant.

status.glance: The general-level valence formula and the old/new theory of `S_k(N, χ)` are done, including stability of both spaces under every `T_n`. Newforms are full Hecke eigenforms with an Euler product, and in weight at least two their coefficient fields are number fields. Eisenstein spanning, the bad-prime eigenvalue cases, Atkin–Li pseudo-eigenvalues, Galois stability, the LMFDB invariants, the dimension formulas and the trace formula are partial. The weight-one integrality argument has not begun.

frontier.name: Novikov ring structure (N1)
frontier.text: — define convolution from the finite-fibre lemma and prove the commutative-ring and R-algebra laws, monomial units and the group-ring embedding as a ring map. Everything downstream in N1 depends on this.

frontier.name: Period-filtration topology and completion (N1)
frontier.text: — the neighbourhoods U_C, completeness, density of truncations and the universal completion property, followed by the coefficient/exponent pushforwards.

frontier.name: Torsion multiplicativity and the determinant line (N4)
frontier.text: — the homology-basis determinant line, multiplicativity for based short exact sequences of acyclic complexes with the Koszul sign, and the long-exact-sequence correction for general complexes. `ofExactLift` is the natural input.

frontier.name: Square-minor formula and scalar extension (N4)
frontier.text: — the projected-minor expression for torsion and its compatibility with field extension and direct sums, needed before torsion can be taken componentwise over total quotient rings.

frontier.name: Closed one-forms and period covers (N2)
frontier.text: — the zero locus, Morse condition and period homomorphism. This depends on the DifferentialGeometry and MorseTheory suppliers named in the README rather than on anything built here.

status.glance: Only the algebraic foundations have begun. The scalar Reidemeister torsion of a based complex over a field is defined, with its basic invariance laws, and the Novikov series carrier exists as an additive group without multiplication. The geometric layers, from closed one-forms and lifted moduli through the Novikov complex, periodic orbits, the dynamical torsion theorem and Euler structures, have not begun.

rows.name: MorseTheory

frontier.name: Cell attachment across a critical level
frontier.text: — the quadratic-model retraction has to be glued into M through disjoint Morse charts and combined with the band deformation. That gives the homotopy equivalence M_{c+ε} ≃ M_{c−ε} ∪ D^λ relative to the lower sublevel.

frontier.name: Regular levels and sublevels as manifolds
frontier.text: — the scalar-level atlas and the boundary atlases for M_a and for bands are still missing. The smooth version of the band product depends on them, and so does the cobordism material.

frontier.name: Exponential convergence on manifolds (M6)
frontier.text: — transport the vector-space Łojasiewicz-type estimate to charts to get dist(γ(t), p) ≤ C·e^{−ct}.

frontier.name: The Lusternik–Schnirelmann bound (M4)
frontier.text: — the critical-level deformation it needs has landed. What remains is the critical-level induction and AlgebraicTopology's categorical-cover supplement.

frontier.name: Morse approximation in the strong topology (M3)
frontier.text: — define the strong C^k neighbourhoods first, then use the compact-exhaustion perturbation argument. Both are untouched.

status.glance: The finite Morse core is in place up to, but not including, cell attachment on a manifold. Critical Hessians, normal forms and critical-free band deformation are proved, and so is trapped gradient convergence without a rate. The handle step exists only in the quadratic model. The CW model, Morse approximation, the Morse inequalities and Morse–Bott theory have not begun.

frontier.name: Weighted diagrams and finiteness (N2.2, N2.4)
frontier.text: — the open orbit of the grade-zero centralizer on 𝔤(2), uniqueness of that orbit, and the resulting injection of nilpotent orbits into weighted diagrams. The {0, 1, 2} bound and [𝔤(0), e] = 𝔤(2) are already in hand. The open-orbit step needs the orbit and differential dictionary from N0.3.

frontier.name: Internal Jordan decomposition (N0.2)
frontier.text: — the semisimple part of a Lie derivation is a derivation, so x = xₛ + xₙ splits inside 𝔤, with uniqueness. Nothing for this has landed.

frontier.name: Type A partitions (N4)
frontier.text: — Jordan-chain bases, recovering the partition from dim ker(Xᵏ), the centralizer dimension Σ(λ′ⱼ)², and dominance for closure order. The SL/GL comparison and the trace-codimension step it needs are done.

frontier.name: Group-level triples (N2.1)
frontier.text: — the algebraic SL₂ homomorphism into G and conjugacy of triples by the unipotent centralizer. This waits on the ReductiveGroups Lie/adjoint dictionary.

frontier.name: The nilpotent cone as a scheme (N1)
frontier.text: — the zero fiber of the adjoint quotient χ, with its complex points identified with the ad-nilpotent elements. This consumes ReductiveGroups 11C and the FormalConnectionsOpers invariant adapter. None of the downstream geometry (N5, N7–N9) can start until it exists.

status.glance: The Lie-algebraic theory of sl₂-triples is in place: Jacobson–Morozov, Kostant's conjugacy of triples, the transverse decomposition behind the Slodowy slice, and the {0, 1, 2} bound on weighted diagrams. All of it is stated for an abstract finite-dimensional Lie algebra in characteristic zero. Nothing algebro-geometric has begun. There is no nilpotent cone as a scheme, no flag variety, no exponential, no Springer resolution and no subregular surfaces.

rows.name: NoncommutativeGeometry

frontier.name: SBI sequence and periodic cohomology
frontier.text: — the remaining N1 algebra. It needs S, defined as exterior product with σ₁, together with I and B on cohomology, exactness at every term, periodic cohomology as a direct limit, and its comparison with the (b, B) totalization at the pinned constants. B and the bicomplex relations are already there.

frontier.name: Algebraic K₀/K₁ and descent of the pairings
frontier.text: — the even pairing currently takes a single idempotent. Building K₀ by group completion and K₁ as GL∞/E∞, then proving invariance under stabilization and conjugation, would turn it into a pairing on K₀. The odd pairing with its (1+i)⁻¹ constant is not started.

frontier.name: Higher universal forms and cycles
frontier.text: — extend one-forms to the graded differential algebra over A⁺, prove d² = 0 and graded Leibniz, and realize cyclic cocycles as characters of cycles, including the nonunital example φ(a,b,c) = abc on ℂ.

frontier.name: Continuous cyclic theory
frontier.text: — Fréchet completeness of the completed projective tensor product, continuous multilinear cochains with the bounded-set topology, and completed bar resolutions. These are prerequisites for the smooth-torus computations in N6.

frontier.name: N3–N7
frontier.text: — not yet begun. N3 depends on the OperatorKTheory Fredholm suppliers, N4 on OperatorIdeals singular values, and N6 on the rotation algebra in OperatorKTheory K7. None of these dependencies has been checked here.

status.glance: The algebraic core of N1 exists for unital algebras, and so does the first piece of N2: cyclic cohomology with Connes' B, the ground-ring computation, reduced and relative variants, and the even pairing with idempotents. The SBI sequence, periodic cohomology, cycles and characters are still missing, and so is all of N3–N7: Fredholm modules, Dixmier traces, spectral triples and the noncommutative torus have not begun.

frontier.name: Exponentials span extreme rays
frontier.text: : the proved direction says that every extreme ray of the completely monotone cone is spanned by some `e^{-pt}`. The converse, that each `e^{-pt}` actually spans an extreme ray, is not stated. It should follow from uniqueness in Hausdorff–Bernstein–Widder.

frontier.name: Handing the resolvent core across
frontier.text: : the README gives the scalar generalization of the shared resolvent core to `OperatorTheory/SelfAdjointSpectralTheory`. The core here is now stated for topological modules over a general ring, so that roadmap can consume it directly. Whether it still needs more is for that roadmap's report.

status.glance: All three parts are done. Every named milestone is proved, and so are two stretch results: Stone's theorem and Bochner's theorem on locally compact abelian groups. The one open item is the converse half of the extreme-ray description of completely monotone functions.

rows.name: OperatorAlgebraDynamics

frontier.name: Integrated form as a *-representation
frontier.text: — prove multiplicativity and the star law for the integrated form of a covariant pair. The README prescribes doing this first for compact-support integrands, then by L¹ approximation.

frontier.name: The twisted L¹ algebra
frontier.text: — prove ‖f*‖₁ = ‖f‖₁ and that the involution is anti-multiplicative for convolution, complete to the Banach *-algebra, and build approximate units. This is the input to the full norm.

frontier.name: Density of entire analytic elements
frontier.text: — Gaussian smearing gives a norm-dense invariant subalgebra. With it, the KMS characterization can be upgraded from the all-entire special case to checking on a dense invariant algebra.

frontier.name: Invariance of β-KMS states for β ≠ 0
frontier.text: and the finite-dimensional Gibbs state — both are self-contained D7 milestones on top of the existing KMS API.

frontier.name: Regular covariant representation and the full crossed product
frontier.text: — the regular representation on L²(G,H), then the full norm via a bounded family of cyclic representations, `A⋊αG`, and its universal property into multiplier algebras.

status.glance: Only the foundations of D1 (actions, multipliers, twisted convolution, integrated forms) and D7 (generators, entire analytic elements, the definition of KMS states) have landed. No crossed product, groupoid algebra, modular-theory comparison or spin-system result exists yet, and D2–D6 and D8–D9 are untouched.

frontier.text: — iterate the one-level lifting theorem down the dimensions. frontier.name: Conjugacy of maximal tori.
frontier.text: The general theorem still assumes that diagonalizable subgroups conjugate into a reference torus. The vector-group step for solvable groups, where [two splittings of a semidirect product by a diagonalizable group are conjugate](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/DiagonalizableGroup/SemidirectProduct.html#TauCeti.Comodule.IsRegularCocycle₁.isConj_pointSplitting), is now in place.

frontier.name: Parabolics as `P(λ)`.
frontier.text: It remains to identify each parabolic `k`-subgroup with some `P(λ)` and to prove that `U(k)` acts transitively on Levi subgroups. [Distinct points of `U(λ)` already give distinct Levi factors](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/Dynamic/Conjugation.html#BialgHom.injOn_conjugate_leviDefiningHopfIdeal). Layer 7b waits on this.

frontier.name: Root datum and Weyl group of a reductive group.
frontier.text: Centralizers of character kernels, with Lie algebra the sum of the root spaces on `ℤα`, are the start of the rank-one root maps. Extracting roots and coroots and identifying `N(T)/T` with the Weyl group remain.

frontier.name: Projective closed orbits.
frontier.text: With closed orbits in hand, Layer 3A next needs properness of the orbit model and the equivariant restriction `V → H⁰(X, O(1))`.

frontier.name: Lang's theorem.
frontier.text: ReductiveGroupsPartII owns it. Nothing here yet applies it to `F`-stable parabolics, unipotent radicals or centralizers, so Layers 7b–7e cannot start.

status.glance: The foundations are done: the group-scheme dictionary, representations as comodules, the Lie algebra, tori and the unipotent radical. Most of the finite-field lane (Layers 7b–7e and 7g), Levi complements in characteristic zero, classification and the spectral Weyl lane have not begun.

rows.name: ReflectionInvariantTheory

frontier.name: Tor′ vanishing for reflection groups
frontier.text: — build a graded free `A`-resolution of `k`, push `δ_s` and multiplication by `ℓ` through to `Tor′_1^A(k,S)`, and use Reynolds invariants on the resolution to show the group is zero. The divided-difference operator and the Hilbert ideal are ready for this.

frontier.name: Forward Shephard–Todd
frontier.text: — from Tor′ vanishing, deduce that `S` is free over `A`, then prove faithfully flat regularity descent and the vertex cotangent-dimension count. That gives polynomiality on `dim V` generators. The regularity-descent lemma is a separate target the README flags explicitly.

frontier.name: Reynolds and scalar extension
frontier.text: — show that the invariant subalgebra and the Reynolds projector commute with base change in the finite-free setting. This is the last named §1 construction, and §3 needs it to move degrees from ℝ to ℂ and from ℚ to ℝ.

frontier.name: Converse Shephard–Todd
frontier.text: — the inertia/stabilizer correspondence in codimension one, purity of the branch locus for the residual map `V/H → V/G`, and triviality of connected finite étale covers of affine space. None of these has been started.

frontier.name: Coinvariant package for real reflection groups
frontier.text: — the Jacobian as a product of reflecting-hyperplane forms, the harmonic complement, freeness of rank `|W|`, and the identities `∏ dᵢ = |W|` and `Σ dᵢ = r + |Ref(W)|`. All of this waits on polynomiality.

status.glance: Most of the finite-group invariant layer (§1) is done: the invariant subalgebra and Reynolds operator, Molien's formula, Noether's finiteness theorem and degree bound. Groundwork for the forward direction of Shephard–Todd has started, but neither direction of the theorem is proved. The real-reflection coinvariant package, the Weyl degree/Coxeter dictionary and the source examples have not begun.

frontier.name: Almost-split sequences
frontier.text: : make the left almost-split map left minimal. Then [the cokernel completion](https://taucetiproject.org/docs/TauCeti/CategoryTheory/AlmostSplit/Completion.html#TauCeti.IsLeftAlmostSplit.isAlmostSplit_cokernelSequence) gives an almost-split sequence ending at every non-projective indecomposable, and the irreducible-morphism quiver becomes a translation quiver.

frontier.name: Brauer–Schur–Weyl duality
frontier.text: : show that the orthogonal Brauer action commutes with `O(n)` and fills its commutant. Then build the symplectic action, whose cap and cup conventions are sign-sensitive.

frontier.name: The Harish-Chandra isomorphism
frontier.text: : show that the projection hits all dot-invariants. With orbit separation already proved, this also gives the converse that equal central characters force one dot orbit.

frontier.name: The Gassmann pair in `S₁₆`
frontier.text: : realise `C₄ × C₄` and `Q₈ × C₂` by their regular actions and use the new cycle-type criterion to show that they are almost conjugate but not conjugate.

frontier.name: Triality for `Spin₈`
frontier.text: : the cyclic intertwiners exist only on Lie-algebra generators over `ℚ`. Still missing are an order-three automorphism of the group and the proof that it is outer.

status.glance: Six roadmaps are complete: root systems, semisimple algebras, compact groups, character theory, modular induction and Ado–Iwasawa. Induction–restriction is complete apart from its Gassmann layers, the first of which is now mostly built. Schur–Weyl duality, the classical groups, highest weight, spin representations, quivers and Lie groups are partial. Affine Weyl geometry, the Fourier form of the Weyl formula, and the Lie-group layers from complexification onward have not begun.

I found nothing yet on Jacobi fields, index theory, comparison geometry, minimal submanifolds, Bochner identities or spherical harmonics.

frontier.name: Laplace transform of the step function
frontier.text: — define `f(t) = a ⌊eᵗ⌋₊` for `t ≥ 0`, prove it is locally integrable using the step partition, and identify its transform on `Re z > 0` with `F(z+1) + H(z)` from `LSeriesHasSum`.

frontier.text: — apply Newman's theorem at `T = log(N+1)`, identify the finite integral with `Σ_{n≤N} a n log(1 + 1/n)`, and subtract the step correction at `0`. The result must be stated as the ordered limit of `Σ_{1≤n≤N} a n / n`.

frontier.name: N2 comparison API
frontier.text: — the real-to-natural cutoff equivalence, finite coefficient changes with explicit corrections, linearity and uniqueness of the endpoint.

frontier.name: N3 coefficients and Euler logarithm
frontier.text: — define `aχ = χ · Λ / log`, prove its values on prime powers and the bound `‖aχ‖ ≤ 1`, and glue local logarithms of `LFunction χ` on balls along `Re s = 1` into a holomorphic extension of the Euler log. This needs N2's endpoint before it can be used.

frontier.name: Ordered Euler product at `1`
frontier.text: — the `Tendsto` of the finite products `∏_{p≤N} (1 − χ(p)/p)⁻¹` to `LFunction χ 1`, plus the finite-deletion variant. Both wait on the item above.

frontier.name: Four-twist labels from geometry (TG2).
frontier.text: Construct the sign lines χ: π₁(C) → {±1} and the twisted normal operators, then define σ(C) and i(C) by determinant transport, so that `torusWeightSeries` is fed actual labels. frontier.name: Disjointness on a square-zero ray.
frontier.text: Prove that distinct relevant torus images on the ray of A₀ are disjoint, by positivity and zero intersection. The independent-component expansion then identifies the ray-only count, and the conditional comparison with the full Gr series follows.

frontier.name: Instantiating `IsGoodCycle` (TG3).
frontier.text: Supply its hypotheses from actual curves: positivity of intersections, singular adjunction ind(C) = d(C) − 2δ(C), and the generic-point dimension bounds. This needs the bounded-window compactness and the stable-map adapter from AnalyticStableMaps.

frontier.name: Weighted count at fixed J.
frontier.text: Build the finite configuration carrier and Gr_(J,ω)(A) as a finite sum, with point-constraint and cutoff independence. This is the first point where the weights become an invariant.

frontier.name: TG11.2 normalization tests.
frontier.text: The integral Wang torsion order |det(I − P)| remains, as does the sign comparison saying the canonical orientation is opposite to the product orientation. The latter depends on the TG0.1 and TG11.2 orientation constructions.

frontier.text: — define `H_n(q)` by generators and relations, prove the `T_w` basis indexed by `Sₙ`, and prove that `H_n(q)` is isomorphic to the stage and injects into the infinite algebra. Almost everything else in H1 is blocked on this.

frontier.name: Existence of the Ocneanu trace
frontier.text: — uniqueness is done. The library's own documentation says existence waits on the basis theorem for the stages.

frontier.name: Jucys-Murphy elements and their tableau eigenvalues
frontier.text: — the content-separation input is ready. What remains is the elements themselves, their commutation, and the eigenvalue `Q^(column−row)` on a fixed Specht basis, which needs the Specht modules first.

frontier.name: The cocenter basis and Ram's formula
frontier.text: — `cycleBlock_cocenterBasis` and the trace-comparison exports. The power-sum basis covers the symmetric-function side, but the Hecke side has not been started.

frontier.name: Atomic tensor models
frontier.text: — the signed R-matrix exists, but the weighted trace on it, and the proof that it gives a positive Markov trace, are open. These need the H3 state carrier to be specified first.

status.glance: The foundations of H1 have started. The infinite Hecke algebra, its stages and its braid homomorphism are in place, and so are the content-separation and power-sum inputs to the module theory. None of H1's main theorems are proved yet: there is no finite presentation, no basis theorem, no Specht modules and no cocenter basis. H2 has uniqueness of Markov traces but not existence. H3 has only its R-matrix building block, and H4 has not begun.

frontier.name: The scalar-curvature transformation law
frontier.text: — specialize the conformal curvature formula to Ricci and scalar curvature for ĝ = u^(4/(n−2))g, and prove Scal_ĝ = u^(−(n+2)/(n−2))L_g u together with the operator identity for L_ĝ. Both inputs (the connection change and the conformal Laplacian) are now present.

frontier.name: Conformal invariance of the Yamabe quotient
frontier.text: — define Q_g and Y(M,[g]), and prove Q_ĝ(v) = Q_g(uv), first for smooth functions and then on the H¹ domain. The weak-domain half waits on Y1's Sobolev carrier.

frontier.name: Cotton and the Weyl–Schouten theorem
frontier.text: — define Cotton, prove the conformal laws and div W = (n−3)C, then use the first-jet Frobenius argument to show that W = 0 (n ≥ 4) or C = 0 (n = 3) characterizes local conformal flatness.

frontier.name: The sharp Euclidean Sobolev inequality
frontier.text: — with the extremals' energy already computed, what remains is the inequality a_n∫|du|² ≥ Y(Sⁿ)‖u‖²_{p_n} on D¹,² and the classification of its equality cases (Y2.1–Y2.2).

frontier.name: Closed-manifold Sobolev interfaces
frontier.text: — Y1's H¹/Lᵖ adapters, compact embeddings and the first eigenvalue of L_g, which depend on the PDE and K5a supplier lanes.

status.glance: Only the foundations have started. Parts of Y0 (conformal tensors) and Y2 (the bubbles of sharp Euclidean Sobolev theory) are in place. The analytic interfaces, the variational and blow-up theory, and every existence theorem (Y1, Y3–Y10) have not begun.

frontier.name: Non-Dynkin trees.
frontier.text: Prove the left-end exactness of the preprojective Koszul complex for affine `Dₙ`, `E₆`, `E₇`, `E₈` and the other non-Dynkin trees, then deduce the Hilbert series and zigzag Koszulity. These trees have no orientation without sinks, so the current argument does not reach them.

frontier.name: The braid group action and `K₀`.
frontier.text: Assemble the proved relations into an action of the Artin braid group on the homotopy category of graded modules, and compare its action on graded `K₀` with the reflection representation.

frontier.name: Spherical twists and transfer.
frontier.text: Prove the Seidel–Thomas type-`A_m` relations and the transfer of the action through a supplied derived equivalence.

frontier.name: Liu–Wang formality.
frontier.text: Prove that the affine `D₄` deformation is nontrivial up to `A∞` isomorphism, then prove the Hochschild comparison and intrinsic formality for trees. This needs derived Koszul duality for `Π₂(Q)`, which has not begun.

frontier.name: Calabi–Yau completions.
frontier.text: Identify `Π₂(Q)` and `Γ₃(Q, W)` with the sibling roadmap's derived and deformed completions. This waits on that roadmap's completion layer.

status.glance: Layers 0–2 are done. On the preprojective side, the finite ADE theory is complete: finite-dimensionality and self-injectivity hold for every orientation. The non-Dynkin theory, meaning Koszul resolutions and the Hilbert series, is proved for every connected graph containing a cycle, but not for the non-Dynkin trees. The braid complexes satisfy their inverse, commutation and braid relations. The Calabi–Yau completion identifications, derived Koszul duality and Liu–Wang formality have not begun.

frontier.text: : the polynomial certificate needs prime degree, so a field such as `ℚ(ζ₈)` is outside it. The README excludes this case from scope, so extending the certificate is new work, not a missing milestone.

frontier.text: : `a` and `a†` exist only on Schwartz space. On `L²` they are unbounded, so extending them needs closed-operator packaging rather than continuous linear maps. The README treats this as a downstream target, not a milestone.

status.glance: Every part of the roadmap is done. The Hermite functions and the Chebyshev polynomials are complete orthonormal bases of their `L²` spaces. Both are built from one family-agnostic layer that also gives the weighted-measure and multidimensional bases. Each basis carries an explicit expansion and Parseval API. The Hermite basis also has its two main structural consequences: it diagonalizes the `L²` Fourier transform, and on Schwartz space it carries the ladder operators. What is left lies outside the roadmap's own targets.

frontier.name: Higher homotopy of spheres, `RPⁿ` and lens spaces.
frontier.text: The covering isomorphism gives `π_k(RPⁿ) ≅ π_k(Sⁿ)` for `k ≥ 2`, but nothing here computes `π_n(Sⁿ)`; that needs a degree or Hurewicz argument, and neither appears here.

frontier.name: Existence of `K(G, 1)` spaces for an arbitrary group.
frontier.text: Only recognition is proved, with circles and tori as examples; constructing one for a given group rests on realization theory the README places outside this roadmap.

frontier.name: Bases without a universal cover.
frontier.text: The standing local hypotheses are shown to be exactly what a simply connected cover requires, so the classification cannot be pushed further as stated; spaces failing them would need a different notion of cover, and nothing here attempts one.

status.glance: Every stage of the roadmap has its stated targets proved. The universal cover is constructed, subgroups of `π₁(X, x₀)` classify connected covers in both pointed and unpointed form, covers are classified categorically with `π₁(X, x₀)` recovered as the automorphisms of the fibre functor, and the application list (`π₁(S¹)`, `π_n(S¹)`, tori, `K(G, 1)` recognition, `RPⁿ`) is complete. What remains lies beyond the roadmap's text: computing higher homotopy groups, and bases without a universal cover.
